topic: What antenna design considerations optimize ground station visibility during short service windows in LEO constellations?
response: To optimize ground station visibility during short service windows in LEO constellations, consider using antennas with narrow beamwidths (half-power beam width, HPBW) to minimize satellite-to-ground distance and increase signal strength. The inclination of 74º and orbit altitude of around 900 km suggest a high latitude area coverage requirement, necessitating antenna designs that compensate for the increased path loss.
reference_context: The reference context discusses LEO constellations with an orbit altitude of around 900 km, inclination of 74º, and zone of subscriber radio visibility above the 7º local horizon. It also mentions the need for high latitude area coverage and satellite service zone radius of more than 2500 km.
